function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.content:
It depends a bit on what *interface* you’re referring to and what platform you’re working on. Below is a quick “cheat‑sheet” of the most common ways to pull detailed interface information, plus a few follow‑up questions that will help me give you the exact steps you need.

---

## 1. Linux / Unix

| Tool | What it shows | Typical command |
|------|---------------|-----------------|
| `ip` | Addresses, MTU, state, link‑layer info, traffic stats | `ip -d addr show eth0` |
| `ifconfig` (legacy) | Same as above, but less verbose | `ifconfig eth0` |
| `ethtool` | Driver, speed/duplex, link status, driver options | `ethtool eth0` |
| `lshw -class network` | Hardware details (driver, bus info, serial number) | `sudo lshw -class network -short` |
| `netstat -i` | Packet counters per interface | `netstat -i` |
| `ss -i` | Per‑socket statistics (useful for troubleshooting) | `ss -i` |
| `psutil` (Python) | Programmatic access to all of the above | `psutil.net_if_addrs()` |

**Example**  
```bash
$ ip -d addr show eth0
2: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
    inet 192.168.1.10/24 brd 192.168.1.255 scope global dynamic eth0
       valid_lft 86399sec preferred_lft 86399sec
    inet6 fe80::21a:2bff:fe3c:4d5e/64 scope link 
```

---

## 2. Windows

| Tool | What it shows | Typical command |
|------|---------------|-----------------|
| `ipconfig /all` | IP, MAC, DHCP, DNS, etc. | `ipconfig /all` |
| `Get-NetAdapter` (PowerShell) | Adapter status, speed, duplex, MAC | `Get-NetAdapter -Name Ethernet0` |
| `Get-NetIPConfiguration` | IP config per adapter | `Get-NetIPConfiguration -InterfaceAlias Ethernet0` |
| `Get-NetAdapterStatistics` | Traffic counters | `Get-NetAdapterStatistics -Name Ethernet0` |
| `wmic nic` | Hardware details | `wmic nic where Name="Ethernet0" get /format:list` |

**Example**  
```powershell
PS C:\> Get-NetAdapter -Name Ethernet0 | Format-List *
Name              : Ethernet0
InterfaceDescription : Intel(R) Ethernet Connection (2) I219-V
Status            : Up
MacAddress        : 00-1A-2B-3C-4D-5E
LinkSpeed         : 1 Gbps
...
```

---

## 3. Cisco IOS / IOS‑XE / IOS‑XR

| Command | What it shows | Typical usage |
|---------|---------------|---------------|
| `show interface GigabitEthernet0/1` | All details: IP, MAC, MTU, speed, duplex, errors, counters | `show interface Gi0/1` |
| `show interface status` | Summary of all interfaces | `show interface status` |
| `show interface counters` | Traffic counters per interface | `show interface counters` |
| `show interface description` | Descriptions set on each interface | `show interface description` |
| `show interface transceiver` | SFP/Transceiver details | `show interface transceiver Gi0/1` |

**Example**  
```text
GigabitEthernet0/1 is up, line protocol is up
  Hardware is iGbE, address is 001a.2b3c.4d5e (bia 001a.2b3c.4d5e)
  MTU 1500 bytes, BW 1000000 Kbit/sec, DLY 10 usec,
     reliability 255/255, txload 1/255, rxload 1/255
  Encapsulation ARPA, loopback not set
  Keepalive set (10 sec)
  Full-duplex, 1000Mb/s, media type is RJ45
  ...
```

---

## 4. Juniper Junos

| Command | What it shows | Typical usage |
|---------|---------------|---------------|
| `show interfaces ge-0/0/1 detail` | Full details: IP, MAC, MTU, speed, errors, counters | `show interfaces ge-0/0/1 detail` |
| `show interfaces terse` | Summary of all interfaces | `show interfaces terse` |
| `show interfaces statistics` | Traffic counters | `show interfaces statistics` |
| `show interfaces diagnostics optics` | Transceiver diagnostics | `show interfaces diagnostics optics ge-0/0/1` |

---

## 5. SNMP (generic)

If you’re managing a fleet of devices, SNMP can pull the same data programmatically:

```bash
snmpwalk -v2c -c public 192.168.1.1 IF-MIB::ifDescr
snmpwalk -v2c -c public 192.168.1.1 IF-MIB::ifInOctets
```

---

## 6. REST APIs / SDKs

Many modern devices expose a REST API that returns JSON with all interface details. For example, a Cisco Meraki dashboard API call:

```http
GET https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/{networkId}/devices/{serial}/interfaces
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

Or a Python library:

```python
import psutil
for iface, addrs in psutil.net_if_addrs().items():
    print(iface, addrs)
```

---

## Quick Checklist

1. **What OS / vendor?**  
   - Linux → `ip`, `ethtool`  
   - Windows → PowerShell cmdlets  
   - Cisco → `show interface`  
   - Juniper → `show interfaces detail`  

2. **What level of detail?**  
   - Basic (IP, MAC, status) → `ip addr`, `ipconfig`  
   - Advanced (errors, counters, transceiver) → `ethtool`, `show interface counters`, `show interfaces diagnostics optics`  

3. **Do you need programmatic access?**  
   - Use SNMP, REST API, or a language library (`psutil`, `netifaces`, `pySNMP`).  

---

### Follow‑Up Questions

1. **Which platform are you on?** (Linux, Windows, Cisco IOS, Juniper, etc.)  
2. **Are you looking for a one‑off manual check, or do you need to automate this?**  
3. **Do you have any specific metrics you care about?** (e.g., error counts, speed, duplex, transceiver health)  

Answering those will let me give you a precise command or script tailored to your environment.
